diagnosis.root_cause: The ONU transmit laser is ageing: TX power has steadily fallen from approximately +2.4 dBm to +2.03 dBm while TX bias current has risen from approximately 11.2 mA to 15.1 mA, exceeding the healthy 9.5-13.0 mA range. RX power, distance, supply voltage, PON peers, OLT, VLAN, and RADIUS state do not indicate another fault.
evidence: The ONU is online, authenticated, responding, and completing the exchange successfully.
RX power is stable around -24 dBm, which is within the normal range, with no progressive optical loss or excessive RX variation.
TX power remains nominal but has declined progressively from roughly +2.4 dBm to +2.03 dBm over the seven-day period.
TX bias current rises progressively from roughly 11.2 mA to 15.1 mA, well above the healthy maximum of 13.0 mA; rising bias at constant or declining TX power is characteristic of laser ageing.
Distance is constant at 241 m, so there is no evidence of a changed fibre path.
Other customers on EPON0/7 have normal online status and optical readings, and the OLT has healthy CPU, memory, temperature, uptime, and all tested PONs.
The ONU has six sessions in 24 hours, which is elevated, but below the eight-session flapping threshold and does not establish authentication flapping.
RADIUS records, line ID, assigned IP, VLAN 1107, router heartbeat, and live probes are consistent, ruling out the principal provisioning, router, VLAN, and authentication faults.

remediation.action: Schedule replacement of the ONU or its optical transmitter. Before replacement, clean and reseat the customer-side optical connector and recheck optical levels; if the elevated bias persists, replace the ONU. Monitor TX power and bias after replacement and investigate the customer sessions separately if they remain elevated.

ground_truth.root_cause: The ONU transmit laser is at end of life. Bias current has risen from 11.4 to 15.1 mA and, over the last two days, output power has begun to fall despite it, meaning compensation is now failing.
expected_reasoning: The customer reports progressive worsening, which fits both fibre degradation and laser degradation
RX sits at -23.9 dBm in the low-normal band and is noisier than the usual floor, but it is flat with no downward trend
TX bias current has climbed from 11.4 to 15.1 mA, well past the 13.0 mA ceiling
TX power held at 2.42 dBm while bias rose, then began falling to 2.05 dBm in the last two days
Falling output despite maximum bias means the laser can no longer compensate
Supply voltage has drifted from 3.45 to 3.36 V, consistent with a failing transmitter
Distance is constant, so there has been no change to the fibre path
Peers on EPON0/7 are normal, so shared infrastructure is not involved
Flat RX with collapsing TX is a transmitter fault, not path attenuation
distractors: RX in the low-normal band with extra noise invites a fibre degradation diagnosis
Steadily declining traffic fits either fault equally well
The complaint wording matches the fibre degradation pattern almost exactly
